raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
The Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 (Quark W4A4) changes for MI355X that touch the same Qwen3.5 GDN layer, its MXFP4 GEMM inputs and
the gated RMSNorm + MXFP4 kernel, in one PR (19 commits plus one merge):

1. Fused GDN prefill prologue (Conv1D, state update, gating) and gated RMSNorm + MXFP4 output epilogue, with the
   strided `in_proj` views. This was the original PR.
2. Ratio-3 fused qkvzba split on AITER/HIP, which the strided views need. Was #43381.
3. GDN `in_proj_qkvz` + `in_proj_ba` packed into one AITER ASM MXFP4 GEMM. Was #43785.
4. Bit-exact fusion of the MXFP4 input quantization into the preceding add + RMSNorm, SiLU-and-mul and attention output
   gate, and the packed `in_proj` at prefill sizes. Was #47154 (which had already absorbed #47155).
5. The GDN output norm + MXFP4 quantization per part of the pipelined chunk scan. Was #47777.

Stacked on #47774, merged in as one merge commit (`651bdf421c`): Part 5 needs #47774's pipelined chunk scan. Review only
the commits listed below; the #47774 commits drop out of this diff once #47774 merges and this branch is rebased.

## Folded-in PRs

#43381, #43785, #47154 and #47777 were open PRs by the same author, stacked on or overlapping with this one. They are
closed in favour of this PR. Their own commits were cherry-picked unchanged (`git cherry-pick -x`); each picked commit
keeps its message, plus the `(cherry picked from commit ...)` line and a `Folded in from #<n> (<sha>)` line. The merge
commits on #47154 and #47777 (they only joined their dependencies) were not carried over. Merging the consolidated
branches gives a source tree byte-identical to merging the separate PRs (checked on the full Qwen3.8 MI355X PR stack), so
the code is the same as reviewed there.

| #43785 | `cb035632dd` | `de950ad4ad` | Pack GDN in_proj_qkvz+ba into one AITER ASM MXFP4 GEMM | decode throughput TP1 +3.4% / TP2 +3.8% (5 serving rows, with the M <= 64 cap, before the rebase) |

| #47154 (from #47155) | `c016002847` | `1cb3d935f2` | Fuse SiLU-and-mul with the down_proj MXFP4 input quant | TTFT -1.7..-1.9%; TPOT -3.1% at 16 concurrent |

| #47777 | `d3d7e72bab` | `17c4e9a589` | GDN output norm + MXFP4 quant per part of the pipelined chunk scan | TTFT -0.30..-0.47% |

TTFT ranges are median TTFT over 100k-200k-token prompts; TPOT is median time per output token at 8k input / 1k output.

There is no single A/B of the whole PR. The rows were measured on a stack that moved between measurements, so they do not
add up exactly. Without the opt-in prologue switch, Parts 1 and 5 do nothing; Parts 3 and 4 need
`SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1`; the SiLU-and-mul fusion also needs ROCm/aiter#7116. Every fused producer writes
the same GEMM input bytes as the unfused path. The one exception is `1c8eda2973`: within one bf16 ulp of `l2norm_fwd` in
2.7 ppm of the elements.

Accuracy of the whole stack: greedy output ids identical on four reference prompts, needle in a haystack 30/30 at
100k-200k tokens, GSM8K-200 0.920-0.960 at TP1 (the run-to-run range of this stack), and 0.935-0.950 at TP2 (all 1,319
questions: 0.923), where the earlier inexact producers had lowered it to 0.880-0.900.

Known test interaction: `test_quark_mxfp4_asm_packed_gpu.py` (Part 3) patches `_use_aiter_asm_fp4_gemm`, which #43360
removes. It passes on this branch alone; with #43360 the test needs a one-line update.

In the parts below, "this PR" means that part, and references to #43381, #43785, #47155, #47154 and #47777 point to the
parts here.

### Part 1 (original #39912): fused GDN prefill prologue and MXFP4 output epilogue

#### Summary

- Fuse the Qwen3.8 TP1 GDN prefill producer’s causal Conv1D, state update, raw contiguous Q/K/V emission, and raw A/B to FP32 g/beta preparation on gfx950.
- Keep Q/K raw at the producer boundary and preserve the existing chunk scan’s `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True` path for exact BF16 behavior.
- Fuse per-head gated RMSNorm with MXFP4 activation quantization before `out_proj`, supporting row-major EVEN output for Triton and native shuffled RoundUp output for the AITER ASM consumer.
- When the prefill prologue is on, read the GDN `in_proj` outputs as strided views (as CUDA already does) instead of unpacking them into contiguous `mixed_qkv` / `z` / `b` / `a` copies, since the prologue and the gated RMSNorm read them in place.
- Keep all additions fail closed: unsupported architecture, topology, dtype, stride, execution mode, state layout, or quantization contract retains the existing path.

#### Modifications

- `qwen3_5.py`: `use_strided_prefill_z` is now also true on ROCm when the new `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet._uses_qwen38_prefill_views` holds, so prefill takes `qwen3_5_gdn_prefill_projection_views` instead of `fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat_contiguous`. The check is a conservative mirror of the prologue's eligibility:
  - prologue enabled (AITER, gfx95, `SGLANG_QWEN38_GDN_PREFILL_PROLOGUE_FUSION=1`);
  - attention TP 1 with the Qwen3.8-27B GDN head layout (16 QK heads, 48 V heads, head dim 128);
  - extend without speculation, without multi-item scoring and without a mamba track mask;
  - not deterministic inference and not page-major KV layout;
  - no DP padding.

  Every other ROCm batch keeps the contiguous unpack, and CUDA behavior is unchanged. If the prologue still declines a batch at runtime, the views go to the stride-aware fallbacks: the Triton `causal_conv1d_fn` (channel-last), `fused_gdn_gating` and the gated-norm kernels. No new env var. The values read are the same, only through views, so the math is unchanged.

#### Changes since the first version

- Rebased onto `main` after #39598 merged (details below).
- Conv1D bias made optional so the prologue actually runs on Qwen3.8 (details below).
- The strided-views change was folded in from #47156.

#### Current state (2026-10-29)

- Rebased onto `main` after [#39598](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39598) (Quark AITER ASM FP4 GEMM) merged; the #39598 commits are no longer part of this branch, which now carries four commits (the fourth is the strided-views change from #47156).
- Includes the Conv1D bias fix (see below), without which the prologue never ran on Qwen3.8.
- Measured split on Qwen3.8-27B MI355X, leave-one-out from our current best image: the prefill prologue (with the bias fix) is worth +1.9 pp at TP1; the MXFP4 output epilogue alone is within noise (+0.1 pp TP1, +0.6 pp TP2).
- On the rebased head, the prologue and epilogue pass their MI355X unit and kernel tests (`test_qwen38_gdn_prefill_prologue.py` 6 passed, `test_qwen3_5_gdn_mxfp4.py` 6 passed), and the stacked TP1 time-to-first-token and accuracy runs (GSM8K, needle in a haystack) run with the prologue on. Their own performance has not yet been re-measured separately on the rebased head; the performance sections below predate the rebase. The strided-views change was measured on MI355X on top of the rebased stack (see "Strided in_proj views" below).

Rebase notes:

- #39598 as merged already accepts a row-major `(x_fp4, x_scales)` tuple and shuffles the scales itself. The ASM-path epilogue output, whose scales are already padded and shuffled, is now tagged as `_AsmShuffledMxfp4Input` so `apply_weights` validates it and passes it through instead of shuffling twice; untagged tuples keep #39598's behavior.
- The GDN gated-norm call now falls through to the epilogue only after `main`'s FP8 small-M path declines.
- The prologue dispatch now lives in `GDNAttnBackend._fused_prefill_prologue`, next to `main`'s `_convolve_prefill` / `_prefill_gates` helpers. It also stays off when a CUDA conv block table is in use.
- `SGLANG_QWEN38_GDN_PREFILL_PROLOGUE_FUSION` is registered in `Envs` (same name and default), and `supports_fused_raw_qk_prefill` has a `False` default on `LinearAttnKernelBase`.
- The ROCm kernel test moved to `test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_rmsnorm_gated_mxfp4.py` after the `test/registered/kernel` -> `kernels` rename.

#### Dependency and scope

[#39598](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39598) has merged; this PR extends its Quark AITER ASM FP4 GEMM input contract.

The prefill producer targets Qwen3.8 TP1 GDN extend layers on gfx950 and is opt-in through `SGLANG_QWEN38_GDN_PREFILL_PROLOGUE_FUSION=1`. Decode, target verification, MIS, page-major state pools, DP padding, tracked-state batches, deterministic inference, and the model’s softmax-attention layers retain their existing paths.

The strided-views change needs #43381 (ratio-3 fused qkvzba split on AITER) to take effect: without it, the Qwen3.8-27B layout (ratio 3) does not reach the fused-unpack branch on ROCm and the change is a no-op. Overlap: #41683 and #47128 switch every ROCm extend to strided views; this PR switches only the batches the Qwen3.8 prologue consumes.

The producer emits raw BF16 post-Conv Q/K because the existing scan’s Q/K L2Norm reduction order is part of the exact numerical contract. V, FP32 g/beta, Conv state updates, packed-varlen boundaries, initial-state behavior, scheduler tails, and scan normalization remain unchanged.

#### Update: Conv1D bias is optional

Qwen3.8 checkpoints have no GDN Conv1D bias, so the earlier eligibility check rejected every real prefill and the fused producer never ran on the target model. The producer now accepts `bias=None` and selects the existing `HAS_BIAS=False` kernel variant, and rank 0 logs once whether the prologue is enabled, or why not. New tests: bias-free output is bit-exact against `causal_conv1d_fn`, and bias shape/dtype/stride mismatches are rejected.

A/B of this fix, MI355X TP1, `amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`, 5 serving rows, same image with and without it: throughput +0.43% geomean, TTFT −8.39% (8K c4 −34.6%), TPOT +0.18%. The performance sections below predate this fix and will be re-measured.

#### Strided in_proj views

Setup: MI355X (gfx950), Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 (`amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`), SGLang TP1 with `--attention-backend aiter`, FP8 KV cache, `--enable-amd-monokernel` and chunked prefill 16384. "With vs without" = the full stack (this change together with the rest of this PR, #43381 and the other Qwen3.8 MI355X PRs) vs the same build without this change, on the same GPU, averaged over 2 GPUs. Prefill: 1 request at a time, 1 output token, 8 prompts after 1 warm-up, mean per-prompt time-to-first-token ratio. Repeat noise of the full stack on one GPU: TTFT 0.1-0.8%; TPOT 0.1-0.8%, except 2.4% at 16 concurrent requests on one GPU.

TP1, with the Qwen3.8 prefill prologue on (`SGLANG_QWEN38_GDN_PREFILL_PROLOGUE_FUSION=1`), with vs without the strided-views change, time to first token:

| Input tokens | Without → with |
|---|---|
| 100k | 3.076 → 3.001 s (-1.8%) |
| 131k | 4.300 → 4.185 s (-2.8%) |
| 200k | 7.690 → 7.517 s (-2.2%) |

Accuracy with the change: TP1 GSM8K-200 0.930 / 0.945 / 0.940 and needle in a haystack 30/30.

#### Correctness

Exact HIP6 parity passes for dense and packed-varlen batches, one/four/sixteen sequences, 64-token and scheduler tails, initial and no-initial state, signed-zero and softplus-threshold gates, raw Q/K/V/g/beta boundaries, Conv state, scan output, recurrent-state updates, packed MXFP4 values, and valid E8M0 scales.

`test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_5_gdn_mxfp4.py` (CPU CI, already registered) gains `TestQwen38PrefillProjectionViews`:

- TP1 Qwen3.8 extend with the prologue on reads views, also when there is no DP metadata;
- 13 cases keep the contiguous unpack: prologue off, deterministic, page-major, TP2, other k/v head counts or dims, decode, target verify, multi-item scoring, mamba state tracking and DP padding.

On MI355X, `test_qwen3_5_gdn_mxfp4.py` (with `TestQwen38PrefillProjectionViews`): 6 passed; `test_qwen38_gdn_prefill_prologue.py` with the strided-views change: 6 passed.

The focused producer test reports the first mismatching index, values, bit patterns, mismatch count, and maximum absolute difference so future compiler regressions localize to raw Conv output, gating, or the unchanged scan normalization boundary.

#### Component accounting

The complete producer-plus-normalization boundary changes from 10 launches to 3 while retaining both existing Q/K L2Norm launches. It removes 82,304 semantic bytes and 41,152 allocation-volume bytes per token/layer.

Across 48 GDN layers at scheduler chunk 16,384, this removes 30.140625 GiB of semantic traffic and 336 launches at 8K, 220.756531 GiB and 1,344 launches at 60K, and 482.25 GiB and 2,688 launches at 128K.

#### Focused performance

Measured on MI355X TP1 using a ROCm image pinned by digest, fixed server arguments, FP8 KV cache, and 16,384-token chunked prefill.

The HIP7 component benchmark reduces prologue latency by 34–36% across `T={8192,10848,13312,16384}` and one/four/sixteen sequences. Launch profiling confirms the 10-to-3 boundary.

Two-direction HIP6/HIP7 serving crossover, reported as the symmetric geometric delta versus the same image with the existing output epilogue but without the new prefill producer:

- 8K input, concurrency 4: output throughput −0.08%; TTFT −3.45%.
- 60K input, concurrency 4: output throughput +1.21%; TTFT −2.54%.
- 60K input, concurrency 16: output throughput +1.96%; TTFT −2.47%.
- 128K input, concurrency 4: output throughput +1.03%; TTFT −1.82%.

The 8K output-throughput metric is decode dominated; the prefill-only optimization is visible in TTFT. Both directions improved 60K and 128K throughput.

#### Full OOB validation

Control and candidate images were pinned by digest; row-level results are available on request. Clean sequential TP1 control/candidate and TP2 control/candidate runs completed all canonical text and image rows without benchmark failures.

Key text deltas are output throughput / TTFT / TPOT:

- TP1 8K/c4: +3.17% / −38.88% / −1.46%.
- TP1 60K/c4: +2.45% / −2.57% / −2.38%.
- TP1 60K/c16: +2.97% / −2.47% / −3.03%.
- TP1 128K/c4: +2.50% / −2.80% / −2.48%.
- TP2 8K/c4: +3.57% / −30.14% / −1.68%.
- TP2 60K/c4: +0.70% / −1.12% / −0.56%.
- TP2 60K/c16: +0.71% / +2.64% / −1.30%.
- TP2 128K/c4: +0.55% / approximately neutral / −0.53%.

The candidate does not yet satisfy the no-regression gate for multimodal workloads. TP2 image throughput regressed on seeds 13, 16, and 17; image TTFT regressed by up to 8.23%; and image TPOT regressed by up to 12.88%. Keep the producer opt-in and do not promote the candidate image as a default until these regressions are resolved and revalidated.

#### Prologue and output-norm speedups (`d6285d8a5a`..`50471725dc`)

Five commits after the strided views (`e27f519c9a`), each one measured on its own. They make the
prologue and the output norm faster. The fused path's math, inputs and outputs are unchanged.

| commit | change | kernel, MI355X, Qwen3.8-27B shapes, 16384 tokens | median TTFT, 100k-200k-token prompts |
|---|---|---|---|
| d6285d8a5 | prologue: wider lanes for the Conv1D launch from 2048 tokens per batch (16 tokens x 256 channels per warp) | 527 -> 364 us | -1.7% to -2.0% |
| 46e75b188 | prologue: dedicated tiled kernel (32 tokens x 256 channels per program) for every batch size | 283.0 -> 243.7 us | -0.06% to -0.42% |
| 1c8eda297 | prologue writes q and k L2-normalized; the chunk kernel skips its own l2norm (`use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=False`) | 300.2 -> 271.2 us (prologue + 2 x `l2norm_fwd`) | -0.23% to -0.43% |
| 4ab77b535 | prologue: tap products rounded with the hardware bf16 convert; conv-state selects only in a sequence's first block | 275.3 -> 246.9 us | -0.22% to -0.56% |
| 50471725d | gated RMSNorm + MXFP4: E2M1 rounding with `v_cvt_scalef32_pk_fp4_f32` on gfx950 | 153 -> 118 us | -0.01% to -0.23% |

Accuracy:
- Commits 1, 2, 4 and 5 are bit-identical. Commit 3 is within one bf16 ulp of `l2norm_fwd`, in 2.7 ppm of the elements
  (reduction order).
- After each commit: greedy output ids identical on four reference prompts (100k-200k tokens and a short one),
  needle-in-a-haystack 30/30 at 100k-200k tokens, GSM8K-200 0.920-0.960 (the run-to-run range of this stack).

Tests (MI355X, this branch):

  kernel's tile edges, the q/k norm and tap products at extreme magnitudes.
- `kernels/ops/layernorm/test_rmsnorm_gated_mxfp4.py`: 6 passed.
- `unit/kernels/test_rmsnorm_gated_mxfp4.py`: 12 passed, 7 subtests.
- `test_quark_mxfp4_asm_prequantized.py`: 8 passed.
- `test_qwen3_5_gdn_mxfp4.py`: 6 passed, 13 subtests.

Setup for the TTFT column:

The prologue's legacy and wide launches of `_causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel` are then unreachable, and I can drop them if you

### Part 2 (was #43381): ratio-3 fused GDN qkvzba split on AITER/HIP

#### Motivation

Qwen3.8-27B (and other dense Qwen3.5-architecture hybrids) use 48 v-heads over 16 k-heads in their GDN layers, a v/k head ratio of 3. #34859 taught `fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat_contiguous` to handle non-power-of-two groups through a per-head walk, and enabled ratio 3 on CUDA. The AITER tuple in `qwen3_5.py` was left at `(1, 2, 4, 8)`. On ROCm, every GDN layer of these models therefore still takes the unfused fallback on every forward pass: `torch.split`, two `.contiguous()` copies, and a `torch.cat`.

The kernel itself has no CUDA-specific code on this path, and the existing ratio-3 unit test is already registered for AMD CI.

#### Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py`: add `3` to `_GDN_FUSED_QKVZBA_RATIOS` when `_use_aiter` is set (`(1, 2, 4, 8)` -> `(1, 2, 3, 4, 8)`), and update the comment. CUDA, CPU and non-AITER HIP are unchanged.

#### Accuracy Tests

The fused kernel is pure data movement. `test/registered/attention/test_gdn_fused_split_head_ratios.py` checks it bit-exactly against plain slicing for ratios 1, 2, 3 and 4. On MI355X (ROCm 7.x, torch 2.11.0+rocm, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`), with this branch's source:

```
test_ratio_1 PASSED
test_ratio_2 PASSED
test_ratio_3 PASSED
test_ratio_4 PASSED
4 passed in 4.12s
```

In the same environment, `sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5._GDN_FUSED_QKVZBA_RATIOS` resolves to `(1, 2, 3, 4, 8)`.

#### Speed Tests and Profiling

This change removes two copies and a concat per GDN layer per forward pass on ROCm for ratio-3 models. That is the same path CUDA already takes for this layout. I have not run an end-to-end benchmark for this one-line routing change.

Related: #31091 generalizes the ratio whitelist for every backend. #43366 (draft) skips the split entirely for batched Triton decode by using strided views. This PR is the minimal fix, so that the ROCm prefill/extend path, and decode outside #43366, matches CUDA.

### Part 3 (was #43785): GDN in_proj_qkvz+ba packed into one AITER ASM MXFP4 GEMM

#### Motivation
With `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1` on gfx950 (#39598), Quark W4A4 MXFP4 GDN layers
run `in_proj_qkvz` on the AITER ASM FP4 GEMM while `in_proj_ba` (N=96) stays on Triton
(N <= 128 guard). At decode that is two quantizations of the same input and two GEMMs per
GDN layer.

#### Modifications
- `pack_asm_fp4_weight_tail()` (Quark MXFP4 scheme): appends a row-major MXFP4 projection
  to one already in ASM layout, padded to whole 256-row tiles and shuffled/swizzled like
  `process_weights_after_loading`. Shuffle and swizzle are local to 16/32 rows, so the
  leading rows are unchanged; whole tiles avoid the partial-tile issue behind the guard.
- `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet`: extends the ROCm packed in_proj path (BF16/FP8) to MXFP4: one
  `per_1x32_f4_quant` + `gemm_a4w4`; `in_proj_qkvz` aliases the packed rows, `in_proj_ba`
  keeps its Triton layout for prefill. Gated by the existing `SGLANG_QWEN35_PACKED_IN_PROJ`;
  online weight updates are refused as for FP8.
- Row cap (second commit): the MXFP4 packed GEMM runs up to M = 256 under CUDA-graph capture
  only; eager forwards (extends, short prefills) keep M <= 64, so they do not JIT extra
  quant/GEMM variants. BF16/FP8 packed paths keep 64.
- `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` forwards `prepare_before_cuda_graph_capture` to the
  backbone so dense VL entry checkpoints pack too.

#39598 has merged; this PR now applies directly on main. Tuned a4w4 configs for the packed N:
ROCm/aiter#6419, M <= 64 only so far (without them `gemm_a4w4` uses its default heuristic: correct, possibly slower).

#### Accuracy / tests
- CPU: packing layout and fallbacks, weight loader.
- gfx950 (added, not yet run on this branch): `test_quark_mxfp4_asm_packed_gpu.py`, packed vs
  separate projections, M in {1,2,7,16,33,64,65,128,200,256}.
- Not yet run: GSM8K with `SGLANG_QWEN35_PACKED_IN_PROJ=0/1` on this branch.

5 serving rows, output throughput geomean vs the same image without this change: TP1 +3.4%
(TPOT -3.4%), TP2 +3.8% (TPOT -4.2%); best row +7.7% / +9.7%. Measured as an overlay on a
downstream image built on #39598, not on bare #39598.

MI355X numbers will be re-measured on the rebased head, including the 256-row graph cap.

### Part 4 (was #47154): bit-exact RMSNorm / SiLU-and-mul + MXFP4 quant fusion

#### Motivation

On MI355X (gfx950), Quark W4A4 MXFP4 Qwen3.5/3.8 dense checkpoints run `qkv_proj`, the dense MLP `gate_up_proj` and `down_proj`, and the packed GDN `in_proj` on the AITER ASM FP4 GEMM (`SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1`). Each of these GEMMs gets its FP4 input from a separate `per_1x32_f4_quant(shuffle=True)` that reads back the bf16 tensor the previous op just wrote:

- `qkv_proj`, `gate_up_proj` and GDN `in_proj` quantize the output of the Gemma add+RMSNorm in front of them;
- `down_proj` quantizes the output of SiluAndMul.

That costs one extra kernel launch and one extra round trip of the activation per projection per layer, which is significant at decode batch sizes. This PR moves the quantization into the producing kernel for both cases, without changing a single bit of the GEMM input.

Bit-exactness is deliberate. AITER already has a fused `act_mul_and_mxfp4_quant`, but by default it quantizes the fp32 `silu(gate) * up` with even-rounded scales. That is valid MXFP4, but it is not the input the unfused path produces; this and a non-bit-exact norm+quant producer we tried first matched only 98.2-99.5% of the fp4 bytes, and on Qwen3.8-27B at TP2 that was enough to move GSM8K (see Accuracy).

#### Modifications

##### Add + RMSNorm + MXFP4 quant (`qkv_proj`, `gate_up_proj`, GDN `in_proj`)

- `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant` (`sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/minimax_m3_rmsnorm.py`): the existing ROCm Triton Gemma add+RMSNorm kernel with an MXFP4 epilogue.
  - It rounds the normed row to bf16, then quantizes it the way `per_1x32_f4_quant` does: RoundUp E8M0 scale, 1e-10 amax floor, E2M1 round-to-nearest-even via `v_cvt_scalef32_pk_fp4_f32`.
  - It writes fp4x2 codes, plus E8M0 scales in the shuffled, 256-row padded layout that the ASM GEMM reads.
- `gemma_rms_norm_uses_rocm_triton()` in `layernorm.py`: true when `GemmaRMSNorm.forward_hip` runs that Triton kernel. That is the bf16 path the fused producer must match bit for bit.
- `qwen3_5.py`:
  - `_GemmaRMSNormMXFP4Quant` and `_gemma_rms_norm_for` replace `input_layernorm` / `post_attention_layernorm` only when all of these hold:
    - AITER on gfx950, with the ROCm Triton Gemma norm;
    - hidden size a multiple of 256 and at most 8192;
    - the consumer is a Quark W4A4 MXFP4 linear.
  - Whether a batch takes the fused path is decided per batch, because the ASM GEMM is selected after weight loading. The fused path requires that the consumer actually runs the ASM GEMM for that batch, and it is never taken under torch.compile, sequence parallelism or DP attention. Otherwise, and for the first layer (no residual), the regular bf16 norm runs.
  - The `(fp4x2, E8M0)` pair is routed to ASM FP4 linears (`_select_fused_ar_input_for_linear`) and to the packed GDN `in_proj` (64 rows eager, 256 under graph capture, same caps as #43785).

##### SiLU-and-mul + MXFP4 quant (`down_proj`)

- `Qwen2MoeMLP._silu_mxfp4_quant_fused` calls `act_mul_and_mxfp4_quant(gate_up, "silu", scaling_mode="roundup", shuffle=True, round_to_input_dtype=True)`:
  - `round_to_input_dtype` makes the kernel quantize `bf16(bf16(silu(gate)) * up)`, which is the tensor SiluAndMul writes;
  - `"roundup"` uses `per_1x32_f4_quant`'s E8M0 scale.
  - The result goes to `down_proj` as `_AsmShuffledMxfp4Input` (from #39912), and `down_proj` validates it before calling `gemm_a4w4`.
- `Qwen2MoeMLP.forward` takes the fused path only for 2-D, non-empty batches when `down_proj.use_aiter_asm_fp4_gemm` is set (decided after weight loading). Every other case keeps SiluAndMul followed by the normal quant.
- `_maybe_enable_silu_mxfp4_quant_fusion` (qwen3_5) turns it on for dense MLPs on ROCm only when both `gate_up_proj` and `down_proj` use `QuarkW4A4MXFP4`, and the installed AITER kernel accepts `round_to_input_dtype`. If the AITER kernel cannot reproduce the unfused bytes, the fusion stays off.

##### Common

- No new env var or kill switch. Both paths are only reachable with the existing opt-in `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1`, and they need no separate switch because the GEMM input is bit-identical to the unfused path.

#### Accuracy

Exactness of both producers:

- Norm: fp4 codes, E8M0 scales and the residual output are byte-identical to `GemmaRMSNorm` (ROCm Triton) followed by `per_1x32_f4_quant(shuffle=True)`, so the GEMM sees exactly the same input as before. They are byte-identical to the unfused add + RMSNorm + `per_1x32_f4_quant_hip` in all 30 cases tested: M 1-16,384, hidden size 5,120; unit, large, tiny and all-zero inputs.
- SiLU-and-mul: the fp4 codes and E8M0 scales (valid rows) equal SiluAndMul + `per_1x32_f4_quant_hip(shuffle=True)` byte for byte, in every case of `test_silu_and_mul_mxfp4_quant.py` (32 passed, MI355X).

End to end, Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 on MI355X with both producers enabled + ROCm/aiter#7116:

- TP1: GSM8K-200 0.930, 0.945 and 0.940; needle in a haystack (100k/131k/200k tokens x 5 depths x 2 passes) 30/30; a chat answer is correct.
- TP2: GSM8K-200 0.935, 0.950, 0.940 and 0.950; all 1,319 questions 0.923; needle 30/30.
- No run had an empty answer.

With the earlier, inexact producers enabled at TP2, GSM8K-200 was 0.880-0.900 with 7-12 empty answers.

#### Speed

Setup: MI355X (gfx950), Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 (`amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`), `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1`. SGLang TP1 with `--attention-backend aiter`, FP8 KV cache, `--enable-amd-monokernel`, chunked prefill 16384, or TP2 with INT4 quick reduce. "With vs without" = the full stack (both producers, the dependencies and the related AMD Qwen3.8 PRs) vs the same build without that producer, on the same GPU, averaged over 2 GPUs. Decode = bench_serving random, 8k input / 1k output tokens; prefill = 1 request at a time, 1 output token. Repeat noise of the full stack on one GPU: TTFT 0.1-0.8%; TPOT 0.1-0.8%, except 2.4% at 16 concurrent requests on one GPU.

TP1, with vs without the add + RMSNorm + MXFP4 producer:
- time to first token at 100k / 131k / 200k tokens: 3.015 → 3.001 s (-0.4%), 4.209 → 4.185 s (-0.6%), 7.559 → 7.517 s (-0.4%);
- median time per output token (8k / 1k): -2.1% at 16 concurrent requests, -1.1% at 64, -0.2% at 256.

TP1, with vs without the SiLU-and-mul + MXFP4 producer:
- time to first token at 100k / 131k / 200k tokens: 3.049 → 3.001 s (-1.8%), 4.266 → 4.185 s (-1.9%), 7.633 → 7.517 s (-1.7%);
- median time per output token (8k / 1k): 8.26 → 8.00 ms (-3.1%) at 16 concurrent requests, 19.15 → 18.75 ms (-2.1%) at 64, 57.46 → 56.83 ms (-1.1%) at 256.

TP2: the two producers together make 100k-200k-token prefill 0.9-1.2% faster than with both fusions off.

#### Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_gemma_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant.py` (gfx950, AMD CI). Byte equality against the unfused chain for:
  - M = 1..16384 at hidden 5120, covering the 32-row scale tiles and the 256-row padding boundaries;
  - hidden 1024 / 2560 / 4096 / 8192;
  - edge blocks: all-zero blocks, blocks below the amax floor, large values, and `(1 + w) == 0`;
  - the Qwen3.5 norm module against `GemmaRMSNorm` + `per_1x32_f4_quant_hip`, including the ASM input validation.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/activation/test_silu_and_mul_mxfp4_quant.py` (gfx950, AMD CI stage-b mi35x). Byte equality of the fused path against SiluAndMul + `per_1x32_f4_quant_hip(shuffle=True)`:
  - M in {1, 7, 8, 9, 64, 255, 256, 257, 870, 2048, 4377, 6553, 16384} x intermediate size in {8704, 17408};
  - edge blocks: all-zero, below the amax floor, large;
  - a check that no scale is NaN (0xFF), and that the output passes the ASM GEMM's prequantized-input validation.
- `test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_5_norm_mxfp4_quant.py` (CPU CI, kernel faked):
  - which norms get the fused path, and the bf16 fallbacks: no residual, `post_residual_addition`, consumer declines the batch, fp16, non-contiguous input;
  - routing of the pair to ASM linears only, and to the packed GDN `in_proj`;
  - the eager and graph-capture row caps.
- `test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_5_silu_mxfp4_quant.py` (CPU, AITER faked):
  - enable conditions: ROCm, both projections MXFP4, AITER importable, `round_to_input_dtype` supported;
  - the exact kernel arguments and output dtypes and shapes;
  - forward routing: fusion off, non-ASM `down_proj`, empty batch and 3-D input all fall back.

Results on MI355X: `test_gemma_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant.py` 53 passed, `test_qwen3_5_norm_mxfp4_quant.py` 9 passed, the existing `test_minimax_m3_rmsnorm.py` 14 passed, `test_silu_and_mul_mxfp4_quant.py` 32 passed, `test_qwen3_5_silu_mxfp4_quant.py` 5 passed.

#### Row walk, output gate fusion, packed in_proj at prefill sizes

Three commits after the SiLU-and-mul fusion, each one measured on its own. They extend the fused
MXFP4 input quantization to the attention output gate, speed up the add + RMSNorm + quant kernel, and run the packed GDN
in_proj at prefill sizes when AITER has tuned rows for it.

| commit | change | kernel, MI355X, Qwen3.8-27B shapes, 16384 tokens | median TTFT, 100k-200k-token prompts |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1d4d9cb6de (was 07182237d) | Gemma add + RMSNorm + MXFP4 quant: `min(m, 2 x CUs)` programs walk the rows with a grid stride and load the next row while they reduce and quantize the current one | 117.4-123.9 -> 110.3 us (hidden 5120) | -0.04% to -0.25% |
| e999b39121 (was a545a5c54) | `fused_sigmoid_mul_mxfp4_quant`: the attention output gate and the o_proj MXFP4 quant in one pass (same bytes as `fused_sigmoid_mul` + `per_1x32_f4_quant(shuffle=True)`) | 131.1-132.7 -> 101.6-102.0 us per full-attention layer | -0.28% to -0.59% |
| fa59b6a2f1 (was 6357d98a3) | the packed in_proj (qkvz + padded ba, one ASM FP4 GEMM) also above 64 / 256 rows, when AITER's a4w4 configs have rows for the packed shape at every `getPaddedM` bucket from 512 to 8192 (checked once at load; otherwise the caps stay) | per GDN layer: ~60 us less than the separate norm, quant and two GEMMs (packed GEMM 625 us vs AITER's default kernel 1596 us without the rows) | -0.20% to -0.43% |

The speedup of commit 3 needs the packed-shape rows of ROCm/aiter#7117. Without them nothing changes. The commit also
updates the existing `test_qwen3_5_norm_mxfp4_quant.py` mock for the new attribute and covers the any-size case.

Accuracy:

- Commit 3 feeds the packed GEMM the same MXFP4 input bytes as the separate path.
- After each commit: greedy output ids identical on four reference prompts (100k-200k tokens and a short one),
  needle-in-a-haystack 30/30 at 100k-200k tokens, GSM8K-200 0.935-0.940 (0.920-0.960 on this stack without them).

### Part 5 (was #47777): GDN output norm + MXFP4 quant per part of the pipelined scan

#### Motivation

With `SGLANG_GDN_CHUNK_PIPELINE=1` (#47775), the GDN chunk scan of a long prefill runs in parts: `chunk_h` of part i runs on
the calling stream while a side stream runs the per-chunk kernels of the parts before and after it. The layer's output then
goes through the gated RMSNorm + MXFP4 quantization (the out_proj input, #39912). That kernel ran over all rows after the
scan, alone on the calling stream: 117 us per layer for a 16384-token chunk on MI355X, 48 GDN layers in Qwen3.8-27B. It is
bound by bandwidth and VALU work (the precise sigmoid takes ~11 VALU instructions per element), and launch shapes gain at
most 4%. So the lever is overlap: the rows of a part are final as soon as the side stream has written that part's output,
while `chunk_h` still runs the next part.

#### Modifications

- `chunk_gated_delta_rule(..., epilogue=None)`: `epilogue(o, start, end)` runs on output rows [start, end) once they are
  final. In the pipelined scan it runs on the side stream after each part's output kernel; the last part (and any padded
  rows after the sequence) runs on the calling stream after the scan. In one pass it runs once over all rows.
- The Triton GDN extend kernel passes `epilogue` on and declares `supports_extend_epilogue`. `GDNAttnBackend` takes
  `linear_attn_epilogue` in `forward_extend` and refuses it for target verify, MIS metadata or kernels without support.
- `RadixLinearAttention`: the owning layer sets `output_epilogue`. A call passes the epilogue's tensors as
  `epilogue_inputs`, and they reach the backend as arguments of the breakable CUDA graph's eager break, like the attention
  inputs (under a breakable prefill graph only the break runs at replay, so the model code cannot hold them between
  breaks). After a padded batch's tail is zeroed, the epilogue covers those rows too.
- Qwen3.5 GDN layer: with the pipelined scan on, the strided prefill views, and an out_proj scheme that takes the fused
  gated-norm input (`QuarkW4A4MXFP4.prepare_fused_rmsnorm_gated_rows`), the layer allocates the out_proj input up front,
  passes (z, FP4 codes, scales) as epilogue inputs and feeds the buffers to out_proj after attention. Otherwise nothing
  changes.
- `rmsnorm_gated_mxfp4_quant_rows` writes token rows [start, end) with the launch of the full row count (same rows per
  program), so the bytes are the same as one launch over all rows. With the ASM-shuffled scale layout a range starts at a
  32-token scale tile.

#### Accuracy Tests

- Bit-identical by construction (the same kernels with the same per-row launch parameters, run on rows once they are
  final). Microbenchmark: FP4 codes, ASM-shuffled scales, the attention output and the final state are bit-identical to the
  current scan + norm at 16384, 12596, 8192 and 16000-in-16384 (padded) tokens.
- New unit tests: the epilogue sees every row once, after it is final (4 parts, 3 parts, padded tail, one pass, two
  sequences; output and state unchanged with and without it); the row writer in any order and from inside a scale tile,
  both scale layouts, bytes equal to one launch; the attention layer hands the inputs to the epilogue and covers padding,
  also through the eager break; the layer only takes the path with the pipeline, a supporting backend and scheme. MI355X,
  this branch: `test_chunk_gated_delta_rule.py` 37 passed, 1 skipped; `test_rmsnorm_gated_mxfp4.py` 7 + 12 passed;
  `test_quark_mxfp4_asm_prequantized.py` 8; `test_qwen3_5_gdn_mxfp4.py` 8; `test_radix_linear_attention.py` 8;
  `test_qwen38_gdn_prefill_prologue.py` 10; `test_mamba_prefill_track_metadata.py` 11.
- Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 end to end on MI355X: greedy output ids identical to the run without the change (4 prompts),
  needle-in-a-haystack 30/30 at 100k-200k tokens, GSM8K-200 0.930 (0.925-0.950 without it, same harness); on 60
  multi-needle prompts of 100k-200k tokens the output ids are identical to the run without the change, all 60.

#### Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X, Qwen3.8-27B GDN shapes (48 heads, K = V = 128), one sequence, pipelined scan + output norm per layer (us, two runs):

| tokens | before | after | change | norm alone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16384 | 1071.5-1075.1 | 1024.6-1025.9 | -47 | 117.2 |
| 12596 | 881.8-883.9 | 838.7-840.0 | -43 | 91.0 |
| 8192 | 596.9-599.8 | 579.0-579.3 | -19 | 58.3 |

End to end: Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 (`amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`), TP1 on one MI355X, `--chunked-prefill-size 16384
--page-size 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --attention-backend aiter --cuda-graph-backend-prefill
breakable` with `SGLANG_GDN_CHUNK_PIPELINE=1`; `python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai-chat --dataset-name
random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --random-output-len 1 --max-concurrency 1 --request-rate inf --num-prompts 32
--warmup-requests 1 --flush-cache`; two GPUs, each running before / after / after / before; mean of the four runs per
setting:

| prompt tokens | median TTFT before (s) | after (s) | change | mean TTFT change | input tok/s before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100000 | 2.421 | 2.411 | -10 ms (-0.42%) | -0.42% | 41,095 | 41,264 |
| 120000 | 3.069 | 3.060 | -9 ms (-0.30%) | -0.34% | 38,268 | 38,398 |
| 140000 | 3.777 | 3.763 | -14 ms (-0.37%) | -0.40% | 37,255 | 37,404 |
| 160000 | 4.538 | 4.517 | -21 ms (-0.46%) | -0.51% | 35,252 | 35,432 |
| 180000 | 5.353 | 5.328 | -25 ms (-0.46%) | -0.39% | 33,655 | 33,786 |
| 200000 | 6.230 | 6.201 | -29 ms (-0.47%) | -0.39% | 32,378 | 32,504 |

On each GPU both runs with the change are faster than both runs without it at every length. In a profile of a 200k-token
request the path from the first `chunk_h` to out_proj shrinks by 56-67 us per GDN layer (more than the microbenchmark's 47
us: the norm's launches beside `chunk_h` cost it up to ~40 us, the removed tail saves 119 us).

detail.body:
The Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 (Quark W4A4) changes for MI355X that touch the same Qwen3.5 GDN layer, its MXFP4 GEMM inputs and
the gated RMSNorm + MXFP4 kernel, in one PR (19 commits plus one merge):

1. Fused GDN prefill prologue (Conv1D, state update, gating) and gated RMSNorm + MXFP4 output epilogue, with the
   strided `in_proj` views. This was the original PR.
2. Ratio-3 fused qkvzba split on AITER/HIP, which the strided views need. Was #43381.
3. GDN `in_proj_qkvz` + `in_proj_ba` packed into one AITER ASM MXFP4 GEMM. Was #43785.
4. Bit-exact fusion of the MXFP4 input quantization into the preceding add + RMSNorm, SiLU-and-mul and attention output
   gate, and the packed `in_proj` at prefill sizes. Was #47154 (which had already absorbed #47155).
5. The GDN output norm + MXFP4 quantization per part of the pipelined chunk scan. Was #47777.

### Part 1 (original #39912): fused GDN prefill prologue and MXFP4 output epilogue

#### Summary

- Fuse the Qwen3.8 TP1 GDN prefill producer’s causal Conv1D, state update, raw contiguous Q/K/V emission, and raw A/B to FP32 g/beta preparation on gfx950.
- Keep Q/K raw at the producer boundary and preserve the existing chunk scan’s `use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True` path for exact BF16 behavior.
- Fuse per-head gated RMSNorm with MXFP4 activation quantization before `out_proj`, supporting row-major EVEN output for Triton and native shuffled RoundUp output for the AITER ASM consumer.
- When the prefill prologue is on, read the GDN `in_proj` outputs as strided views (as CUDA already does) instead of unpacking them into contiguous `mixed_qkv` / `z` / `b` / `a` copies, since the prologue and the gated RMSNorm read them in place.
- Keep all additions fail closed: unsupported architecture, topology, dtype, stride, execution mode, state layout, or quantization contract retains the existing path.

#### Modifications

- `qwen3_5.py`: `use_strided_prefill_z` is now also true on ROCm when the new `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet._uses_qwen38_prefill_views` holds, so prefill takes `qwen3_5_gdn_prefill_projection_views` instead of `fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat_contiguous`. The check is a conservative mirror of the prologue's eligibility:
  - prologue enabled (AITER, gfx95, `SGLANG_QWEN38_GDN_PREFILL_PROLOGUE_FUSION=1`);
  - attention TP 1 with the Qwen3.8-27B GDN head layout (16 QK heads, 48 V heads, head dim 128);
  - extend without speculation, without multi-item scoring and without a mamba track mask;
  - not deterministic inference and not page-major KV layout;
  - no DP padding.

  Every other ROCm batch keeps the contiguous unpack, and CUDA behavior is unchanged. If the prologue still declines a batch at runtime, the views go to the stride-aware fallbacks: the Triton `causal_conv1d_fn` (channel-last), `fused_gdn_gating` and the gated-norm kernels. No new env var. The values read are the same, only through views, so the math is unchanged.

### Part 2 (was #43381): ratio-3 fused GDN qkvzba split on AITER/HIP

#### Motivation

Qwen3.8-27B (and other dense Qwen3.5-architecture hybrids) use 48 v-heads over 16 k-heads in their GDN layers, a v/k head ratio of 3. #34859 taught `fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat_contiguous` to handle non-power-of-two groups through a per-head walk, and enabled ratio 3 on CUDA. The AITER tuple in `qwen3_5.py` was left at `(1, 2, 4, 8)`. On ROCm, every GDN layer of these models therefore still takes the unfused fallback on every forward pass: `torch.split`, two `.contiguous()` copies, and a `torch.cat`.

The kernel itself has no CUDA-specific code on this path, and the existing ratio-3 unit test is already registered for AMD CI.

#### Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5.py`: add `3` to `_GDN_FUSED_QKVZBA_RATIOS` when `_use_aiter` is set (`(1, 2, 4, 8)` -> `(1, 2, 3, 4, 8)`), and update the comment. CUDA, CPU and non-AITER HIP are unchanged.

#### Accuracy Tests

The fused kernel is pure data movement. `test/registered/attention/test_gdn_fused_split_head_ratios.py` checks it bit-exactly against plain slicing for ratios 1, 2, 3 and 4. On MI355X (ROCm 7.x, torch 2.11.0+rocm, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`), with this branch's source:

```
test_ratio_1 PASSED
test_ratio_2 PASSED
test_ratio_3 PASSED
test_ratio_4 PASSED
4 passed in 4.12s
```

In the same environment, `sglang.srt.models.qwen3_5._GDN_FUSED_QKVZBA_RATIOS` resolves to `(1, 2, 3, 4, 8)`.

#### Speed Tests and Profiling

This change removes two copies and a concat per GDN layer per forward pass on ROCm for ratio-3 models. That is the same path CUDA already takes for this layout. I have not run an end-to-end benchmark for this one-line routing change.

Related: #31091 generalizes the ratio whitelist for every backend. #43366 (draft) skips the split entirely for batched Triton decode by using strided views. This PR is the minimal fix, so that the ROCm prefill/extend path, and decode outside #43366, matches CUDA.

### Part 3 (was #43785): GDN in_proj_qkvz+ba packed into one AITER ASM MXFP4 GEMM

#### Motivation
With `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1` on gfx950 (#39598), Quark W4A4 MXFP4 GDN layers
run `in_proj_qkvz` on the AITER ASM FP4 GEMM while `in_proj_ba` (N=96) stays on Triton
(N <= 128 guard). At decode that is two quantizations of the same input and two GEMMs per
GDN layer.

#### Modifications
- `pack_asm_fp4_weight_tail()` (Quark MXFP4 scheme): appends a row-major MXFP4 projection
  to one already in ASM layout, padded to whole 256-row tiles and shuffled/swizzled like
  `process_weights_after_loading`. Shuffle and swizzle are local to 16/32 rows, so the
  leading rows are unchanged; whole tiles avoid the partial-tile issue behind the guard.
- `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet`: extends the ROCm packed in_proj path (BF16/FP8) to MXFP4: one
  `per_1x32_f4_quant` + `gemm_a4w4`; `in_proj_qkvz` aliases the packed rows, `in_proj_ba`
  keeps its Triton layout for prefill. Gated by the existing `SGLANG_QWEN35_PACKED_IN_PROJ`;
  online weight updates are refused as for FP8.
- Row cap (second commit): the MXFP4 packed GEMM runs up to M = 256 under CUDA-graph capture
  only; eager forwards (extends, short prefills) keep M <= 64, so they do not JIT extra
  quant/GEMM variants. BF16/FP8 packed paths keep 64.
- `Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration` forwards `prepare_before_cuda_graph_capture` to the
  backbone so dense VL entry checkpoints pack too.

#39598 has merged; this PR now applies directly on main. Tuned a4w4 configs for the packed N:
ROCm/aiter#6419, M <= 64 only so far (without them `gemm_a4w4` uses its default heuristic: correct, possibly slower).

#### Accuracy / tests
- CPU: packing layout and fallbacks, weight loader.
- gfx950 (added, not yet run on this branch): `test_quark_mxfp4_asm_packed_gpu.py`, packed vs
  separate projections, M in {1,2,7,16,33,64,65,128,200,256}.
- Not yet run: GSM8K with `SGLANG_QWEN35_PACKED_IN_PROJ=0/1` on this branch.

#### Benchmark
Earlier measurement (M <= 64 cap, before the rebase): MI355X, amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4,
5 serving rows, output throughput geomean vs the same image without this change: TP1 +3.4%
(TPOT -3.4%), TP2 +3.8% (TPOT -4.2%); best row +7.7% / +9.7%. Measured as an overlay on a
downstream image built on #39598, not on bare #39598.

MI355X numbers will be re-measured on the rebased head, including the 256-row graph cap.

### Part 4 (was #47154): bit-exact RMSNorm / SiLU-and-mul + MXFP4 quant fusion

#### Motivation

On MI355X (gfx950), Quark W4A4 MXFP4 Qwen3.5/3.8 dense checkpoints run `qkv_proj`, the dense MLP `gate_up_proj` and `down_proj`, and the packed GDN `in_proj` on the AITER ASM FP4 GEMM (`SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1`). Each of these GEMMs gets its FP4 input from a separate `per_1x32_f4_quant(shuffle=True)` that reads back the bf16 tensor the previous op just wrote:

- `qkv_proj`, `gate_up_proj` and GDN `in_proj` quantize the output of the Gemma add+RMSNorm in front of them;
- `down_proj` quantizes the output of SiluAndMul.

That costs one extra kernel launch and one extra round trip of the activation per projection per layer, which is significant at decode batch sizes. This PR moves the quantization into the producing kernel for both cases, without changing a single bit of the GEMM input.

Bit-exactness is deliberate. AITER already has a fused `act_mul_and_mxfp4_quant`, but by default it quantizes the fp32 `silu(gate) * up` with even-rounded scales. That is valid MXFP4, but it is not the input the unfused path produces; this and a non-bit-exact norm+quant producer we tried first matched only 98.2-99.5% of the fp4 bytes, and on Qwen3.8-27B at TP2 that was enough to move GSM8K (see Accuracy).

#### Modifications

##### Add + RMSNorm + MXFP4 quant (`qkv_proj`, `gate_up_proj`, GDN `in_proj`)

- `gemma_fused_add_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant` (`sglang/kernels/ops/layernorm/minimax_m3_rmsnorm.py`): the existing ROCm Triton Gemma add+RMSNorm kernel with an MXFP4 epilogue.
  - It rounds the normed row to bf16, then quantizes it the way `per_1x32_f4_quant` does: RoundUp E8M0 scale, 1e-10 amax floor, E2M1 round-to-nearest-even via `v_cvt_scalef32_pk_fp4_f32`.
  - It writes fp4x2 codes, plus E8M0 scales in the shuffled, 256-row padded layout that the ASM GEMM reads.
- `gemma_rms_norm_uses_rocm_triton()` in `layernorm.py`: true when `GemmaRMSNorm.forward_hip` runs that Triton kernel. That is the bf16 path the fused producer must match bit for bit.
- `qwen3_5.py`:
  - `_GemmaRMSNormMXFP4Quant` and `_gemma_rms_norm_for` replace `input_layernorm` / `post_attention_layernorm` only when all of these hold:
    - AITER on gfx950, with the ROCm Triton Gemma norm;
    - hidden size a multiple of 256 and at most 8192;
    - the consumer is a Quark W4A4 MXFP4 linear.
  - Whether a batch takes the fused path is decided per batch, because the ASM GEMM is selected after weight loading. The fused path requires that the consumer actually runs the ASM GEMM for that batch, and it is never taken under torch.compile, sequence parallelism or DP attention. Otherwise, and for the first layer (no residual), the regular bf16 norm runs.
  - The `(fp4x2, E8M0)` pair is routed to ASM FP4 linears (`_select_fused_ar_input_for_linear`) and to the packed GDN `in_proj` (64 rows eager, 256 under graph capture, same caps as #43785).

##### SiLU-and-mul + MXFP4 quant (`down_proj`)

- `Qwen2MoeMLP._silu_mxfp4_quant_fused` calls `act_mul_and_mxfp4_quant(gate_up, "silu", scaling_mode="roundup", shuffle=True, round_to_input_dtype=True)`:
  - `round_to_input_dtype` makes the kernel quantize `bf16(bf16(silu(gate)) * up)`, which is the tensor SiluAndMul writes;
  - `"roundup"` uses `per_1x32_f4_quant`'s E8M0 scale.
  - The result goes to `down_proj` as `_AsmShuffledMxfp4Input` (from #39912), and `down_proj` validates it before calling `gemm_a4w4`.
- `Qwen2MoeMLP.forward` takes the fused path only for 2-D, non-empty batches when `down_proj.use_aiter_asm_fp4_gemm` is set (decided after weight loading). Every other case keeps SiluAndMul followed by the normal quant.
- `_maybe_enable_silu_mxfp4_quant_fusion` (qwen3_5) turns it on for dense MLPs on ROCm only when both `gate_up_proj` and `down_proj` use `QuarkW4A4MXFP4`, and the installed AITER kernel accepts `round_to_input_dtype`. If the AITER kernel cannot reproduce the unfused bytes, the fusion stays off.

##### Common

- No new env var or kill switch. Both paths are only reachable with the existing opt-in `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1`, and they need no separate switch because the GEMM input is bit-identical to the unfused path.

#### Accuracy

Exactness of both producers:

- Norm: fp4 codes, E8M0 scales and the residual output are byte-identical to `GemmaRMSNorm` (ROCm Triton) followed by `per_1x32_f4_quant(shuffle=True)`, so the GEMM sees exactly the same input as before. They are byte-identical to the unfused add + RMSNorm + `per_1x32_f4_quant_hip` in all 30 cases tested: M 1-16,384, hidden size 5,120; unit, large, tiny and all-zero inputs.
- SiLU-and-mul: the fp4 codes and E8M0 scales (valid rows) equal SiluAndMul + `per_1x32_f4_quant_hip(shuffle=True)` byte for byte, in every case of `test_silu_and_mul_mxfp4_quant.py` (32 passed, MI355X).

End to end, Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 on MI355X with both producers enabled + ROCm/aiter#7116:

- TP1: GSM8K-200 0.930, 0.945 and 0.940; needle in a haystack (100k/131k/200k tokens x 5 depths x 2 passes) 30/30; a chat answer is correct.
- TP2: GSM8K-200 0.935, 0.950, 0.940 and 0.950; all 1,319 questions 0.923; needle 30/30.
- No run had an empty answer.

With the earlier, inexact producers enabled at TP2, GSM8K-200 was 0.880-0.900 with 7-12 empty answers.

#### Speed

Setup: MI355X (gfx950), Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 (`amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`), `SGLANG_ROCM_USE_AITER_FP4_ASM_GEMM=1`. SGLang TP1 with `--attention-backend aiter`, FP8 KV cache, `--enable-amd-monokernel`, chunked prefill 16384, or TP2 with INT4 quick reduce. "With vs without" = the full stack (both producers, the dependencies and the related AMD Qwen3.8 PRs) vs the same build without that producer, on the same GPU, averaged over 2 GPUs. Decode = bench_serving random, 8k input / 1k output tokens; prefill = 1 request at a time, 1 output token. Repeat noise of the full stack on one GPU: TTFT 0.1-0.8%; TPOT 0.1-0.8%, except 2.4% at 16 concurrent requests on one GPU.

TP1, with vs without the add + RMSNorm + MXFP4 producer:
- time to first token at 100k / 131k / 200k tokens: 3.015 → 3.001 s (-0.4%), 4.209 → 4.185 s (-0.6%), 7.559 → 7.517 s (-0.4%);
- median time per output token (8k / 1k): -2.1% at 16 concurrent requests, -1.1% at 64, -0.2% at 256.

TP1, with vs without the SiLU-and-mul + MXFP4 producer:
- time to first token at 100k / 131k / 200k tokens: 3.049 → 3.001 s (-1.8%), 4.266 → 4.185 s (-1.9%), 7.633 → 7.517 s (-1.7%);
- median time per output token (8k / 1k): 8.26 → 8.00 ms (-3.1%) at 16 concurrent requests, 19.15 → 18.75 ms (-2.1%) at 64, 57.46 → 56.83 ms (-1.1%) at 256.

TP2: the two producers together make 100k-200k-token prefill 0.9-1.2% faster than with both fusions off.

#### Tests

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/layernorm/test_gemma_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant.py` (gfx950, AMD CI). Byte equality against the unfused chain for:
  - M = 1..16384 at hidden 5120, covering the 32-row scale tiles and the 256-row padding boundaries;
  - hidden 1024 / 2560 / 4096 / 8192;
  - edge blocks: all-zero blocks, blocks below the amax floor, large values, and `(1 + w) == 0`;
  - the Qwen3.5 norm module against `GemmaRMSNorm` + `per_1x32_f4_quant_hip`, including the ASM input validation.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/activation/test_silu_and_mul_mxfp4_quant.py` (gfx950, AMD CI stage-b mi35x). Byte equality of the fused path against SiluAndMul + `per_1x32_f4_quant_hip(shuffle=True)`:
  - M in {1, 7, 8, 9, 64, 255, 256, 257, 870, 2048, 4377, 6553, 16384} x intermediate size in {8704, 17408};
  - edge blocks: all-zero, below the amax floor, large;
  - a check that no scale is NaN (0xFF), and that the output passes the ASM GEMM's prequantized-input validation.
- `test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_5_norm_mxfp4_quant.py` (CPU CI, kernel faked):
  - which norms get the fused path, and the bf16 fallbacks: no residual, `post_residual_addition`, consumer declines the batch, fp16, non-contiguous input;
  - routing of the pair to ASM linears only, and to the packed GDN `in_proj`;
  - the eager and graph-capture row caps.
- `test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen3_5_silu_mxfp4_quant.py` (CPU, AITER faked):
  - enable conditions: ROCm, both projections MXFP4, AITER importable, `round_to_input_dtype` supported;
  - the exact kernel arguments and output dtypes and shapes;
  - forward routing: fusion off, non-ASM `down_proj`, empty batch and 3-D input all fall back.

Results on MI355X: `test_gemma_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant.py` 53 passed, `test_qwen3_5_norm_mxfp4_quant.py` 9 passed, the existing `test_minimax_m3_rmsnorm.py` 14 passed, `test_silu_and_mul_mxfp4_quant.py` 32 passed, `test_qwen3_5_silu_mxfp4_quant.py` 5 passed.

#### Row walk, output gate fusion, packed in_proj at prefill sizes

Three commits after the SiLU-and-mul fusion, each one measured on its own. They extend the fused
MXFP4 input quantization to the attention output gate, speed up the add + RMSNorm + quant kernel, and run the packed GDN
in_proj at prefill sizes when AITER has tuned rows for it.

| commit | change | kernel, MI355X, Qwen3.8-27B shapes, 16384 tokens | median TTFT, 100k-200k-token prompts |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1d4d9cb6de (was 07182237d) | Gemma add + RMSNorm + MXFP4 quant: `min(m, 2 x CUs)` programs walk the rows with a grid stride and load the next row while they reduce and quantize the current one | 117.4-123.9 -> 110.3 us (hidden 5120) | -0.04% to -0.25% |
| e999b39121 (was a545a5c54) | `fused_sigmoid_mul_mxfp4_quant`: the attention output gate and the o_proj MXFP4 quant in one pass (same bytes as `fused_sigmoid_mul` + `per_1x32_f4_quant(shuffle=True)`) | 131.1-132.7 -> 101.6-102.0 us per full-attention layer | -0.28% to -0.59% |
| fa59b6a2f1 (was 6357d98a3) | the packed in_proj (qkvz + padded ba, one ASM FP4 GEMM) also above 64 / 256 rows, when AITER's a4w4 configs have rows for the packed shape at every `getPaddedM` bucket from 512 to 8192 (checked once at load; otherwise the caps stay) | per GDN layer: ~60 us less than the separate norm, quant and two GEMMs (packed GEMM 625 us vs AITER's default kernel 1596 us without the rows) | -0.20% to -0.43% |

The speedup of commit 3 needs the packed-shape rows of ROCm/aiter#7117. Without them nothing changes. The commit also
updates the existing `test_qwen3_5_norm_mxfp4_quant.py` mock for the new attribute and covers the any-size case.

Accuracy:
- Commits 1 and 2 are bit-identical: FP4 codes, scales and the residual sum.
- Commit 3 feeds the packed GEMM the same MXFP4 input bytes as the separate path.
- After each commit: greedy output ids identical on four reference prompts (100k-200k tokens and a short one),
  needle-in-a-haystack 30/30 at 100k-200k tokens, GSM8K-200 0.935-0.940 (0.920-0.960 on this stack without them).

Tests (MI355X, this branch), all passed:

| file | result |
|---|---|
| `test_gemma_rmsnorm_mxfp4_quant.py` (incl. the new row-loop test) | 73 passed |
| `test_sigmoid_mul_mxfp4_quant.py` (new) | 45 passed |
| `test_silu_and_mul_mxfp4_quant.py` | 32 passed |

Setup for the TTFT column:
- Model and server: Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 (`amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`), one MI355X, TP1, chunked prefill 16384, FP8
  KV cache.
- Client: `python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai-chat --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0
  --random-output-len 1 --max-concurrency 1 --request-rate inf --num-prompts 32 --warmup-requests 1 --flush-cache`.
- Each commit was measured on the same GPU against the build without it, before / after / after / before.
- Median TTFT before / after at 100k and 200k:
  - commit 1: 2.487 / 2.485 s and 6.386 / 6.383 s (at the resolution of this benchmark; in a 200k-token profile the
    kernel goes from 15.64 to 14.61 ms per 16384-token chunk);
  - commit 2: 2.521 / 2.512 s and 6.461 / 6.444 s;
  - commit 3: 2.792 / 2.780 s and 7.147 / 7.126 s.

### Part 5 (was #47777): GDN output norm + MXFP4 quant per part of the pipelined scan

#### Motivation

With `SGLANG_GDN_CHUNK_PIPELINE=1` (#47775), the GDN chunk scan of a long prefill runs in parts: `chunk_h` of part i runs on
the calling stream while a side stream runs the per-chunk kernels of the parts before and after it. The layer's output then
goes through the gated RMSNorm + MXFP4 quantization (the out_proj input, #39912). That kernel ran over all rows after the
scan, alone on the calling stream: 117 us per layer for a 16384-token chunk on MI355X, 48 GDN layers in Qwen3.8-27B. It is
bound by bandwidth and VALU work (the precise sigmoid takes ~11 VALU instructions per element), and launch shapes gain at
most 4%. So the lever is overlap: the rows of a part are final as soon as the side stream has written that part's output,
while `chunk_h` still runs the next part.

#### Modifications

- `chunk_gated_delta_rule(..., epilogue=None)`: `epilogue(o, start, end)` runs on output rows [start, end) once they are
  final. In the pipelined scan it runs on the side stream after each part's output kernel; the last part (and any padded
  rows after the sequence) runs on the calling stream after the scan. In one pass it runs once over all rows.
- The Triton GDN extend kernel passes `epilogue` on and declares `supports_extend_epilogue`. `GDNAttnBackend` takes
  `linear_attn_epilogue` in `forward_extend` and refuses it for target verify, MIS metadata or kernels without support.
- `RadixLinearAttention`: the owning layer sets `output_epilogue`. A call passes the epilogue's tensors as
  `epilogue_inputs`, and they reach the backend as arguments of the breakable CUDA graph's eager break, like the attention
  inputs (under a breakable prefill graph only the break runs at replay, so the model code cannot hold them between
  breaks). After a padded batch's tail is zeroed, the epilogue covers those rows too.
- Qwen3.5 GDN layer: with the pipelined scan on, the strided prefill views, and an out_proj scheme that takes the fused
  gated-norm input (`QuarkW4A4MXFP4.prepare_fused_rmsnorm_gated_rows`), the layer allocates the out_proj input up front,
  passes (z, FP4 codes, scales) as epilogue inputs and feeds the buffers to out_proj after attention. Otherwise nothing
  changes.
- `rmsnorm_gated_mxfp4_quant_rows` writes token rows [start, end) with the launch of the full row count (same rows per
  program), so the bytes are the same as one launch over all rows. With the ASM-shuffled scale layout a range starts at a
  32-token scale tile.

#### Accuracy Tests

- Bit-identical by construction (the same kernels with the same per-row launch parameters, run on rows once they are
  final). Microbenchmark: FP4 codes, ASM-shuffled scales, the attention output and the final state are bit-identical to the
  current scan + norm at 16384, 12596, 8192 and 16000-in-16384 (padded) tokens.
- New unit tests: the epilogue sees every row once, after it is final (4 parts, 3 parts, padded tail, one pass, two
  sequences; output and state unchanged with and without it); the row writer in any order and from inside a scale tile,
  both scale layouts, bytes equal to one launch; the attention layer hands the inputs to the epilogue and covers padding,
  also through the eager break; the layer only takes the path with the pipeline, a supporting backend and scheme. MI355X,
  this branch: `test_chunk_gated_delta_rule.py` 37 passed, 1 skipped; `test_rmsnorm_gated_mxfp4.py` 7 + 12 passed;
  `test_quark_mxfp4_asm_prequantized.py` 8; `test_qwen3_5_gdn_mxfp4.py` 8; `test_radix_linear_attention.py` 8;
  `test_qwen38_gdn_prefill_prologue.py` 10; `test_mamba_prefill_track_metadata.py` 11.
- Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 end to end on MI355X: greedy output ids identical to the run without the change (4 prompts),
  needle-in-a-haystack 30/30 at 100k-200k tokens, GSM8K-200 0.930 (0.925-0.950 without it, same harness); on 60
  multi-needle prompts of 100k-200k tokens the output ids are identical to the run without the change, all 60.

#### Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X, Qwen3.8-27B GDN shapes (48 heads, K = V = 128), one sequence, pipelined scan + output norm per layer (us, two runs):

| tokens | before | after | change | norm alone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16384 | 1071.5-1075.1 | 1024.6-1025.9 | -47 | 117.2 |
| 12596 | 881.8-883.9 | 838.7-840.0 | -43 | 91.0 |
| 8192 | 596.9-599.8 | 579.0-579.3 | -19 | 58.3 |

End to end: Qwen3.8-27B MXFP4 (`amd/Qwen3.8-27B-Quark-AWQ-MXFP4`), TP1 on one MI355X, `--chunked-prefill-size 16384
--page-size 1 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --attention-backend aiter --cuda-graph-backend-prefill
breakable` with `SGLANG_GDN_CHUNK_PIPELINE=1`; `python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai-chat --dataset-name
random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --random-output-len 1 --max-concurrency 1 --request-rate inf --num-prompts 32
--warmup-requests 1 --flush-cache`; two GPUs, each running before / after / after / before; mean of the four runs per
setting:

| prompt tokens | median TTFT before (s) | after (s) | change | mean TTFT change | input tok/s before | after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 100000 | 2.421 | 2.411 | -10 ms (-0.42%) | -0.42% | 41,095 | 41,264 |
| 120000 | 3.069 | 3.060 | -9 ms (-0.30%) | -0.34% | 38,268 | 38,398 |
| 140000 | 3.777 | 3.763 | -14 ms (-0.37%) | -0.40% | 37,255 | 37,404 |
| 160000 | 4.538 | 4.517 | -21 ms (-0.46%) | -0.51% | 35,252 | 35,432 |
| 180000 | 5.353 | 5.328 | -25 ms (-0.46%) | -0.39% | 33,655 | 33,786 |
| 200000 | 6.230 | 6.201 | -29 ms (-0.47%) | -0.39% | 32,378 | 32,504 |

On each GPU both runs with the change are faster than both runs without it at every length. In a profile of a 200k-token
request the path from the first `chunk_h` to out_proj shrinks by 56-67 us per GDN layer (more than the microbenchmark's 47
us: the norm's launches beside `chunk_h` cost it up to ~40 us, the removed tail saves 119 us).

detail.title: [Perf] [AMD] qwen3_5: Qwen3.8 GDN and MXFP4 fusions on gfx950 (GDN prefill prologue and output epilogue, packed in_proj, bit-exact norm / SiLU quant fusion)

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,366 @@
+"""Qwen3.8 TP1 GDN prefill-prologue component and launch benchmark.
+
+Run only on an isolated gfx950 device. This reports producer-only latency plus
+the existing Q/K L2Norm suffix, then stops before the rest of the unchanged
+chunked gated-delta scan.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import itertools
+import json
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+import torch
+import triton
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.l2norm import l2norm_fwd
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.linear.fused_gdn_gating import fused_gdn_gating
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.triton_gdn_fused_proj import (
+    fused_qkvzba_split_reshape_cat_contiguous,
+    qwen3_5_gdn_prefill_projection_views,
+)
+from sglang.kernels.ops.mamba.causal_conv1d_triton import (
+    QWEN38_GDN_HEAD_DIM,
+    QWEN38_GDN_NUM_QK_HEADS,
+    QWEN38_GDN_NUM_V_HEADS,
+    QWEN38_GDN_QKV_DIM,
+    causal_conv1d_fn,
+    qwen38_gdn_prefill_prologue,
+)
+
+QKVZ_DIM = QWEN38_GDN_QKV_DIM + QWEN38_GDN_NUM_V_HEADS * QWEN38_GDN_HEAD_DIM
+BA_DIM = 2 * QWEN38_GDN_NUM_V_HEADS
+
+
+def _sequence_lengths(tokens: int, num_sequences: int) -> list[int]:
+    quotient, remainder = divmod(tokens, num_sequences)
+    if quotient == 0:
+        raise ValueError("tokens must be at least num_sequences")
+    return [
+        quotient + (sequence_idx < remainder) for sequence_idx in range(num_sequences)
+    ]

+"""Static semantic-traffic accounting for Qwen3.8 TP1 GDN prefill."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import math
+
+BF16_BYTES = 2
+FP32_BYTES = 4
+Q_WIDTH = 2048
+K_WIDTH = 2048
+V_WIDTH = 6144
+Z_WIDTH = 6144
+GATE_WIDTH = 48
+QKV_WIDTH = Q_WIDTH + K_WIDTH + V_WIDTH
+LAYERS = 48
+SCHEDULER_CHUNK = 16384
+
+
+def _per_token() -> dict[str, dict[str, int]]:
+    # Exact pinned SGLANG_USE_AITER ratio-3 path:
+    #   cat Q/K/V + contiguous B/A, Conv1D output, contiguous Q/K/V,
+    #   and FP32 g/beta. Q/K L2Norm stays inside the scan in both paths.
+    pinned_allocated = (
+        QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES
+        + 2 * GATE_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES
+        + QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES
+        + QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES
+        + 2 * GATE_WIDTH * FP32_BYTES
+    )
+    fused_allocated = QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES + 2 * GATE_WIDTH * FP32_BYTES
+
+    # Reads + writes at semantic tensor widths; parameter-vector reads in the
+    # gating calculation are counted per token, matching the kernel contract.
+    gating_traffic = (
+        2 * GATE_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES
+        + 2 * GATE_WIDTH * FP32_BYTES
+        + 2 * GATE_WIDTH * FP32_BYTES
+    )
+    pinned_traffic = (
+        2 * QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES
+        + 4 * GATE_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES
+        + 2 * QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES
+        + 2 * QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES
+        + gating_traffic
+    )
+    fused_traffic = 2 * QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES + gating_traffic
+    views_traffic = (
+        2 * QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES + 2 * QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES + gating_traffic
+    )
+    views_allocated = (
+        QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES + QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES + 2 * GATE_WIDTH * FP32_BYTES
+    )
+    fused_unpack_traffic = (
+        2 * (QKV_WIDTH + Z_WIDTH + 2 * GATE_WIDTH) * BF16_BYTES
+        + 2 * QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES
+        + 2 * QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES
+        + gating_traffic
+    )
+    fused_unpack_allocated = (
+        (QKV_WIDTH + Z_WIDTH + 2 * GATE_WIDTH) * BF16_BYTES
+        + QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES
+        + QKV_WIDTH * BF16_BYTES
+        + 2 * GATE_WIDTH * FP32_BYTES
+    )
+
+    return {
+        "pinned": {
+            "semantic_bytes": pinned_traffic,
+            "allocated_bytes": pinned_allocated,
+            "launches": 8,
+            "allocations": 9,
+        },
+        "fused": {
+            "semantic_bytes": fused_traffic,
+            "allocated_bytes": fused_allocated,
+            "launches": 1,
+            "allocations": 5,
+        },
+        "removed": {
+            "semantic_bytes": pinned_traffic - fused_traffic,
+            "allocated_bytes": pinned_allocated - fused_allocated,
+            "launches": 7,
+            "allocations": 4,
+        },
+        "alternate_baselines": {
+            "projection_views": {
+                "semantic_bytes": views_traffic,
+                "allocated_bytes": views_allocated,
+                "launches": 5,
+                "allocations": 6,
+            },
+            "fused_unpack": {
+                "semantic_bytes": fused_unpack_traffic,
+                "allocated_bytes": fused_unpack_allocated,
+                "launches": 6,
+                "allocations": 10,
+            },
+        },
+    }
+
+
+def _shape(tokens: int, layers: int, scheduler_chunk: int) -> dict[str, object]:
+    per_token = _per_token()
+    scheduler_passes = math.ceil(tokens / scheduler_chunk)
+    removed = per_token["removed"]
+    return {
+        "tokens": tokens,
+        "layers": layers,
+        "scheduler_chunk": scheduler_chunk,
+        "scheduler_passes": scheduler_passes,
+        "removed": {
+            "semantic_bytes": removed["semantic_bytes"] * tokens * layers,
+            "semantic_gib": (removed["semantic_bytes"] * tokens * layers / (1024**3)),
+            "allocated_bytes": removed["allocated_bytes"] * tokens * layers,
+            "allocated_gib": (removed["allocated_bytes"] * tokens * layers / (1024**3)),
+            "launches": removed["launches"] * layers * scheduler_passes,
+            "allocation_objects": (removed["allocations"] * layers * scheduler_passes),
+        },
+    }
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--tokens", type=int, nargs="+", default=[8192, 60000, 131072])
+    parser.add_argument("--layers", type=int, default=LAYERS)
+    parser.add_argument("--scheduler-chunk", type=int, default=SCHEDULER_CHUNK)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    print(
+        json.dumps(
+            {
+                "per_token": _per_token(),
+                "shapes": [
+                    _shape(tokens, args.layers, args.scheduler_chunk)
+                    for tokens in args.tokens
+                ],
+            },
+            indent=2,
+        )
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+
+"""Fused per-head gated RMSNorm and MXFP4 activation quantization."""
+
+import torch
+import triton
+import triton.language as tl
+
+from sglang.kernels.ops.attention.fla.layernorm_gated import calc_rows_per_block
+from sglang.srt.utils import cdiv, device_context, is_gfx95_supported
+
+MXFP4_BLOCK_SIZE = 32
+MXFP4_ROUND_UP = 1
+MXFP4_ROUND_EVEN = 2
+_MXFP4_SHUFFLE_GROUP_MULTIPLE = 8
+# Shuffled E8M0 scales are stored in tiles of 32 token rows.
+_MXFP4_SHUFFLE_TOKEN_TILE = 32
+
+
+def mxfp4_scale_shape(
+    num_rows: int, num_groups: int, *, shuffle: bool
+) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """Return the row-major or AITER ASM scale-buffer shape."""
+    if not shuffle:
+        return num_rows, num_groups
+    return cdiv(num_rows, 256) * 256, cdiv(num_groups, 8) * 8
+
+
+def _is_mxfp4_shuffled_width_supported(input_size: int) -> bool:
+    """Check AITER ASM's eight-scale-group activation row alignment.
+
+    The shuffled public producer uses its padded scale-group count as the
+    packed-activation row pitch, so a contiguous output is valid only when
+    K/32 needs no padding to the next eight-group tile.
+    """
+    return (
+        input_size > 0
+        and input_size % (MXFP4_BLOCK_SIZE * _MXFP4_SHUFFLE_GROUP_MULTIPLE) == 0
+    )
+
+
+def _is_rmsnorm_gated_mxfp4_layout_supported(
+    x: torch.Tensor,
+    z: torch.Tensor,
+    weight: torch.Tensor,
+    *,
+    num_heads: int,
+    activation: str,
+    shuffle_scales: bool = False,
+) -> bool:
+    """Check the shape, dtype, and strides required by the fused kernel."""
+    if x.ndim != 2 or z.ndim not in (2, 3) or weight.ndim != 1:
+        return False
+    if num_heads <= 0 or x.shape[0] == 0 or x.shape[0] % num_heads != 0:
+        return False
+
+    head_dim = x.shape[1]
+    if (
+        head_dim == 0
+        or head_dim % MXFP4_BLOCK_SIZE != 0
+        or head_dim > 65536 // x.element_size()
+    ):
+        return False
+    if x.dtype not in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16) or z.dtype != x.dtype:
+        return False

+def _mxfp4_quantize(
+    x,
+    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
+    FP4_BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,
+    ROUND_MODE: tl.constexpr,
+    ROUND_UP_MODE: tl.constexpr,
+    PK_FP4_CVT: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Quantize FP32 rows into packed E2M1 values plus E8M0 scales."""
+    num_groups: tl.constexpr = BLOCK_N // FP4_BLOCK_SIZE
+    x = tl.reshape(x, [BLOCK_M, num_groups, FP4_BLOCK_SIZE])
+    amax = tl.max(tl.abs(x), axis=-1, keep_dims=True)
+
+    if ROUND_MODE == ROUND_UP_MODE:
+        # AITER's default MX mode: ceil_pow2(amax / 6), with the same nonzero
+        # floor used by dynamic_per_group_scaled_quant.
+        amax = tl.maximum(amax, 1.0e-10)
+        scale_bits = (amax * (1.0 / 6.0)).to(tl.uint32, bitcast=True)
+        scale_exp = (scale_bits >> 23) & 0xFF
+        has_mantissa = (scale_bits & 0x7FFFFF) != 0
+        scale_exp += (has_mantissa & (scale_exp < 0xFF)).to(tl.uint32)
+        scale = (scale_exp << 23).to(tl.float32, bitcast=True)
+        scale_e8m0 = scale_exp.to(tl.uint8)
+        quant_scale = 1.0 / scale
+    else:
+        # AITER dynamic_mxfp4_quant's Quark-EVEN mode.
+        rounded = amax.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True)
+        rounded = (rounded + 0x200000).to(tl.uint32, bitcast=True) & 0xFF800000
+        rounded = rounded.to(tl.float32, bitcast=True)
+        scale_unbiased = tl.floor(tl.log2(rounded)) - 2
+        scale_unbiased = tl.clamp(scale_unbiased, min=-127, max=127)
+        scale_e8m0 = scale_unbiased.to(tl.uint8) + 127
+        quant_scale = tl.exp2(-scale_unbiased)
+
+    if PK_FP4_CVT:
+        # gfx950 rounds a pair of values to E2M1 in one instruction, the same
+        # byte as the bit arithmetic below for every non-NaN input.
+        lo, hi = tl.split(tl.reshape(x * quant_scale, [BLOCK_M, num_groups, 16, 2]))
+        packed = tl.inline_asm_elementwise(
+            "v_cvt_scalef32_pk_fp4_f32 $0, $1, $2, $3",
+            "=v,v,v,v",
+            args=[lo, hi, 1.0],
+            dtype=tl.int32,
+            is_pure=True,
+            pack=1,
+        ).to(tl.uint8)
+        packed = packed.reshape(BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N // 2)
+    else:
+        qx = (x * quant_scale).to(tl.uint32, bitcast=True)
+
+        sign = qx & 0x80000000
+        qx = qx ^ sign
+        qx_fp32 = qx.to(tl.float32, bitcast=True)
+
+        saturate_mask = qx_fp32 >= 6.0
+        denormal_mask = (~saturate_mask) & (qx_fp32 < 1.0)
+        normal_mask = ~(saturate_mask | denormal_mask)

+        denorm_exp: tl.constexpr = (127 - 1) + (23 - 1) + 1
+        denorm_mask_int: tl.constexpr = denorm_exp << 23
+        denorm_mask_float: tl.constexpr = tl.cast(
+            denorm_mask_int, tl.float32, bitcast=True
+        )
+        denormal_x = (qx_fp32 + denorm_mask_float).to(tl.uint32, bitcast=True)
+        denormal_x = (denormal_x - denorm_mask_int).to(tl.uint8)
+
+        mantissa_odd = (qx >> (23 - 1)) & 1
+        rounding_bias: tl.constexpr = ((1 - 127) << 23) + (1 << 21) - 1
+        # qx has had its sign bit removed, so signed arithmetic can apply the
+        # negative exponent-bias adjustment without an unsigned wraparound.
+        normal_x = qx.to(tl.int32, bitcast=True)
+        normal_x = normal_x + rounding_bias + mantissa_odd.to(tl.int32)
+        normal_x = (normal_x >> (23 - 1)).to(tl.uint8)

+        e2m1 = tl.full(qx.type.get_block_shapes(), 0x7, dtype=tl.uint8)

+        e2m1 = tl.where(denormal_mask, denormal_x, e2m1)

+        e2m1 = tl.reshape(e2m1, [BLOCK_M, num_groups, 16, 2])
+        evens, odds = tl.split(e2m1)
+        packed = (evens | (odds << 4)).reshape(BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N // 2)

+    X,
+    Z,
+    W,
+    Out,

+    HEAD_DIM: tl.constexpr,

+    ROWS_PER_BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    FP4_BLOCK_SIZE: tl.constexpr,

+    ACTIVATION: tl.constexpr,
+    ROUND_MODE: tl.constexpr,

+            token_rows[:, None] * stride_z_token + head_rows[:, None] * stride_z_head

+    else:
+        z_row_offsets = rows[:, None] * stride_z_row
+    z = tl.load(
+        Z + z_row_offsets + cols[None, :],
+        mask=mask,
+        other=0.0,
+    ).to(tl.float32)

+    else:
+        y *= tl.sigmoid(z)

+        y,
+        BLOCK_M=ROWS_PER_BLOCK,
+        BLOCK_N=BLOCK_N,
+        FP4_BLOCK_SIZE=FP4_BLOCK_SIZE,
+        ROUND_MODE=ROUND_MODE,
+        ROUND_UP_MODE=ROUND_UP_MODE,
+        PK_FP4_CVT=PK_FP4_CVT,
+    )
+
+    packed_cols = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N // 2)
+    packed_mask = (rows[:, None] < num_head_rows) & (
+        packed_cols[None, :] < HEAD_DIM // 2
+    )

+        Out + rows[:, None] * (HEAD_DIM // 2) + packed_cols[None, :],
+        packed,
+        mask=packed_mask,
+    )

+    groups_per_head: tl.constexpr = HEAD_DIM // FP4_BLOCK_SIZE
+    block_groups: tl.constexpr = BLOCK_N // FP4_BLOCK_SIZE

+        local_groups[None, :] < groups_per_head

+            (token_rows[:, None] // 32 * SCALE_N_PAD) * 32

+            + ((token_rows[:, None] % 32) // 16)

+    A_log_ptr,
+    a_ptr,  # (tokens, NUM_V_HEADS)
+    b_ptr,
+    dt_bias_ptr,
+    stride_x_token,
+    stride_w_dim,
+    stride_state_seq,
+    stride_state_dim,
+    stride_state_token,
+    stride_a_token,
+    stride_b_token,
+    pad_slot_id: tl.constexpr,
+    HAS_BIAS: tl.constexpr,
+    KERNEL_WIDTH: tl.constexpr,
+    NUM_QK_HEADS: tl.constexpr,
+    NUM_V_HEADS: tl.constexpr,
+    HEAD_DIM: tl.constexpr,
+    NORMALIZE_QK: tl.constexpr,
+    L2NORM_EPS: tl.constexpr,
+    SOFTPLUS_THRESHOLD: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Conv1D + SiLU of a BLOCK_M x BLOCK_N (token, channel) tile of one
+    sequence, written as q, k or v; value blocks also write their heads' gates.
+
+    The per-element math is _causal_conv1d_fwd_kernel's FUSE_QWEN38_GDN_PREP
+    path (same tap order and BF16 products, same rounding point), so q, k, v,
+    g, beta and the conv state are bit-identical to it. With NORMALIZE_QK, q
+    and k leave L2-normalized per head as l2norm_fwd would normalize them.
+    """
+    tl.static_assert(KERNEL_WIDTH == 4)
+    STATE_LEN: tl.constexpr = KERNEL_WIDTH - 1
+    QK_DIM: tl.constexpr = NUM_QK_HEADS * HEAD_DIM
+    V_DIM: tl.constexpr = NUM_V_HEADS * HEAD_DIM

+    i_blk = tl.program_id(1)
+    feat0 = tl.program_id(2) * BLOCK_N
+
+    seq_start = tl.load(query_start_loc_ptr + i_seq).to(tl.int64)
+    seqlen = (tl.load(query_start_loc_ptr + i_seq + 1) - seq_start).to(tl.int32)
+    t0 = i_blk * BLOCK_M
+    if t0 >= seqlen:
+        return
+    cache_idx = tl.load(cache_indices_ptr + i_seq).to(tl.int64)
+    if cache_idx == pad_slot_id:
+        return
+    has_init = tl.load(has_initial_state_ptr + i_seq).to(tl.int1)
+
+    # 64-bit scalar bases per tile; offsets inside the tile stay 32-bit.
+    offs_m = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)
+    offs_n = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N)
+    rows = t0 + offs_m
+    in_seq = rows < seqlen
+    tile_start = seq_start + t0
+    x_tile = x_ptr + tile_start * stride_x_token + feat0
+    state_base = (
+        conv_states_ptr + cache_idx * stride_state_seq + feat0 * stride_state_dim
+    )
+    # The conv state (the KERNEL_WIDTH - 1 = 3 tokens before the sequence, zeros
+    # without an initial state) is read by the sequence's first block only, as
+    # three channel vectors that stand in for the taps' rows before the start.
+    first = i_blk == 0
+    state_cols = state_base + offs_n * stride_state_dim
+    state_mask = (offs_n < BLOCK_N) & first & has_init

+    s1 = tl.load(state_cols + stride_state_token, mask=state_mask, other=0.0)
+    s2 = tl.load(state_cols + 2 * stride_state_token, mask=state_mask, other=0.0)
+
+    if HAS_BIAS:
+        acc = (
+            tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N), dtype=tl.float32)
+            + tl.load(bias_ptr + feat0 + offs_n).to(tl.float32)[None, :]
+        )
+    else:
+        acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N), dtype=tl.float32)
+    # Tap j multiplies the token 3 - j places back (the Conv1D kernel's order).
+    for j in tl.static_range(KERNEL_WIDTH):
+        back = KERNEL_WIDTH - 1 - j
+        src = rows - back
+        xj = tl.load(
+            x_tile + (offs_m - back)[:, None] * stride_x_token + offs_n[None, :],
+            mask=((src >= 0) & in_seq)[:, None],
+            other=0.0,
+        )

+        # per program) keeps the selects out of every other block.
+        if first:
+            if back >= 1:
+                xj = tl.where((src == -1)[:, None], s2[None, :], xj)
+            if back >= 2:
+                xj = tl.where((src == -2)[:, None], s1[None, :], xj)
+            if back >= 3:
+                xj = tl.where((src == -3)[:, None], s0[None, :], xj)

+        # The BF16 product x * w as a bf16 * bf16 multiply gives it: exact in
+        # fp32 (8-bit significands), rounded once to BF16. Spelled out so that
+        # gfx950's convert instruction does the rounding; the implicit BF16
+        # multiply rounds with integer ops (~5 VALU per element and tap), and
+        # this kernel is VALU-bound. Same bits.

+        acc += prod.to(tl.float32)

+                y.to(tl.float32), (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N // HEAD_DIM, HEAD_DIM)
+            )
